blocks.text: Release overview

iOS 13.0 was publicly released on September 19, 2019. iOS 13.0 was the iPhone-only public launch of the annual platform release, centered on Dark Mode, redesigned Photos tools, privacy, maps, and system performance.
The release introduced a systemwide dark appearance, expanded photo and video editing, Sign in with Apple, and broad changes to Maps, Find My, Reminders, Mail, and other built-in apps.
Release overview

iOS 13.1 was publicly released on September 24, 2019. iOS 13.1 followed the initial iPhone launch with Ultra Wideband AirDrop direction, Shortcuts automations, Maps ETA sharing, and additional maintenance.
The release activated U1-assisted AirDrop on the iPhone 11 family, added personal and home automation triggers, and expanded navigation and battery-management behavior.
Release overview
iOS 13.1.1 was publicly released on September 27, 2019. iOS 13.1.1 was a rapid corrective release for restore, battery, Siri, Safari, Reminders, and third-party extension behavior.
Apple documented targeted reliability fixes and one CVE-tracked sandbox correction affecting third-party app extensions.
Release overview
iOS 13.1.2 was publicly released on September 30, 2019. iOS 13.1.2 was a maintenance patch for backup status, Camera, flashlight, display calibration, HomePod Shortcuts, and Bluetooth.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 13.2 was publicly released on October 28, 2019. iOS 13.2 added Deep Fusion on supported iPhone 11 models, AirPods Pro support, new emoji, HomeKit security features, and Siri privacy controls.
The point release combined camera processing and accessory support with HomeKit Secure Video, router controls, and new controls over Siri recordings and history.
Release overview
iOS 13.3 was publicly released on December 10, 2019. iOS 13.3 expanded Screen Time parental controls and refined News, Stocks, Safari security-key support, Photos, Mail, and other system behavior.
Communication Limits was the headline consumer feature, accompanied by updated News presentation and support for FIDO2-compliant external security keys in Safari.
Release overview

iOS 13.3.1 was publicly released on January 28, 2020. iOS 13.3.1 corrected Communication Limits, Mail, FaceTime, notifications, CarPlay, and other reliability issues while adding a U1 location-services control.
The patch mixed privacy and parental-control corrections with communications, camera, Wi-Fi notification, and in-car audio fixes.
Release overview
iOS 13.4 was publicly released on March 24, 2020. iOS 13.4 added iCloud Drive folder sharing, new Memoji stickers, universal app purchases, Mail controls, and a broad maintenance set.
The release expanded collaboration in Files, cross-platform purchases for participating apps, Mail conversation controls, AR Quick Look audio, and Arabic predictive typing.
Release overview
iOS 13.4.1 was publicly released on April 7, 2020. iOS 13.4.1 was a focused maintenance patch for legacy FaceTime interoperability and a Bluetooth quick-action problem.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 13.5 was publicly released on May 20, 2020. iOS 13.5 adapted authentication and communications behavior for the early COVID-19 period and introduced the Exposure Notification API.
The release accelerated access to the passcode field when a mask was detected, enabled public-health exposure-notification apps, and added a Group FaceTime prominence control.
Release overview
iOS 13.5.1 was publicly released on June 1, 2020. iOS 13.5.1 was a single-issue security release addressing a kernel vulnerability.
Apple’s consumer note describes the update as important security maintenance, and the advisory identifies CVE-2020-9859.
Release overview
iOS 13.6 was publicly released on July 15, 2020. iOS 13.6 added digital car keys, Apple News audio, Health symptom tracking, and more granular automatic-update controls.
The release paired new Wallet and media capabilities with health logging, device-management refinements, keyboard corrections, and a broad security set.
Release overview
iOS 13.7 was publicly released on September 1, 2020. iOS 13.7 added an app-less opt-in path for Exposure Notifications in participating jurisdictions and included other iPhone bug fixes.

blocks.text: Release overview

The audited iPadOS 13.0 record is superseded and has no public appearance. Apple previewed the newly named platform in June, but Apple’s public availability record begins with iPadOS 13.1 on September 24, 2019.
No release-event overlay or structured public-release change is created for 13.0. Its prerelease milestones remain untouched, and the public iPadOS launch content belongs to 13.1.
Release overview

iPadOS 13.1 was publicly released on September 24, 2019. iPadOS 13.1 was the first public iPadOS release, establishing an iPad-specific platform identity with redesigned multitasking, Home Screen, Files, Safari, and Apple Pencil workflows.
Apple announced iPadOS as available on September 24 with multiwindow app workflows, a denser Home Screen, external storage, desktop-class browsing, and a redesigned Apple Pencil toolset.
Release overview

iPadOS 13.2 was publicly released on October 28, 2019. iPadOS 13.2 is represented conservatively as a security-bearing public update because the verified iPhone release-note page is not used as an iPad feature source.
The shared Apple advisory explicitly covers supported iPads and documents a broad CVE-tracked correction set; iPhone-only features such as Deep Fusion are not carried onto this iPad event.
Release overview
iPadOS 13.3 was publicly released on December 10, 2019. iPadOS 13.3 is represented with the public date and security content Apple explicitly scoped to supported iPads.
The batch does not transfer the iPhone update page’s consumer feature list to iPadOS without a platform-specific first-party note.
Release overview
iPadOS 13.4 was publicly released on March 24, 2020. iPadOS 13.4 introduced systemwide mouse and trackpad support designed for the iPad interface and expanded iCloud collaboration.
Apple announced a March 24 release with a transforming pointer, Multi-Touch trackpad gestures, broad mouse support, and iCloud folder sharing.
Release overview
iPadOS 13.5 was publicly released on May 20, 2020. iPadOS 13.5 is represented with the public date and security content Apple explicitly scoped to supported iPads.
Face ID mask behavior and the iPhone Exposure Notification description are not assigned to iPadOS; only the shared advisory-backed correction set is included.
Release overview
iPadOS 13.6 was publicly released on July 15, 2020. iPadOS 13.6 is represented with the public date and security content Apple explicitly scoped to supported iPads.
Digital car keys and Health symptom logging from the iPhone notes are not projected onto iPad; the shared advisory supplies the supported platform evidence.
Release overview
iPadOS 13.7 was publicly released on September 1, 2020. The local iPadOS 13.7 public appearance is anchored to Apple’s September 1 index row, whose available-for list includes supported iPads.

events.summary: iOS 13.0 reached the public release channel on September 19, 2019. iOS 13.0 was the iPhone-only public launch of the annual platform release, centered on Dark Mode, redesigned Photos tools, privacy, maps, and system performance. blocks.text: Public release
Apple’s dated release record places iOS 13.0 on September 19, 2019. This article records that public appearance only and does not assign cumulative version notes to any preceding beta.
What changed
The release introduced a systemwide dark appearance, expanded photo and video editing, Sign in with Apple, and broad changes to Maps, Find My, Reminders, Mail, and other built-in apps.

changes.canonicalSummary: Dark Mode adds a systemwide dark color scheme with scheduling and Control Center controls.
